page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-90 is a high-memory general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor providing 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 45 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 720.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The underlying processor includes vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-core compute capability. The instance recorded a multi-core stress-ng result of 129,140.9 and a PassMark CPU score of 87,517.3, both placing in the top ten percent of evaluated systems. High-concurrency operations show similar strength, demonstrated by a Clang software compilation score of 60,172.0 and a ray tracing score of 99,342.0 in Geekbench tests. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, achieving 6,374.57 GB/sec in small-block cached read operations and 218.2 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads, while PassMark database operations reached 28,335.01.

The hardware configuration does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, nor does it supply bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent disk throughput and IOPS rely entirely on attached cloud storage networks. While large-block write memory throughput and single-core execution metrics benchmark within average ranges, the extensive core count and memory pool deliver solid resource density for scale-up computing.

The c3d-highmem-90 is well suited for large in-memory databases, Redis deployments, continuous integration compilation tasks, multi-threaded scientific simulations, and CPU-based LLM inference preprocessing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-90 is a memory-oriented server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 90 dedicated vCPUs across 45 physical cores, 720.0 GB of memory, and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance incorporates no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying on networked block devices for all disk operations. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute capabilities in the top tier, highlighted by high scores in PassMark CPU tests, Clang compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks, alongside strong database and Redis operational throughput. Memory bandwidth remains high for cached reads at 6,374.57 GB/sec, though single-core execution and write bandwidth align with median performance levels. This server profile is designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications, distributed cache clusters, large database operations, and high-concurrency compilation pipelines.
